topic.title: R. Vaishali's FIDE Women's Candidates Win 2026

subtopics.title: Vaishali's Candidates win
subtopics.summary: R. Vaishali won the FIDE Women's Candidates Tournament 2026 in Nicosia, Cyprus, by defeating Kateryna Lagno of Russia in the final round. She finished with 8.5 out of 14 points and became the first Indian woman to claim the Candidates title. Her next challenge is the Women's World Chess Championship against Ju Wenjun of China, later in 2026.

subtopics.title: India's world titles and milestones
subtopics.summary: Indian players hold several major chess titles. Viswanathan Anand won the FIDE World Chess Championship five times, and Gukesh Dommaraju became world champion in 2024 as the second Indian to win the title. Divya Deshmukh and Pranav Venkatesh added to India's record in 2025, and Koneru Humpy has a 2019 world rapid title.

subtopics.title: FIDE, the global chess body
subtopics.summary: FIDE (Fédération Internationale des Échecs), the International Chess Federation, is the global governing authority for chess. Founded in Paris in 1924, it oversees major international competitions and sets rules and rating standards. Its headquarters is in Lausanne, Switzerland, and Arkady Dvorkovich is its President.

subtopics.title: Chess history and records
subtopics.summary: Chess has a long history, from its origin as 'Chaturanga' in Northern India during the Gupta Empire to the World Chess Championship, first contested in 1886. Recent events include India hosting the Chess World Cup 2025 in Goa and India's first-ever Olympiad gold in 2024. Several records involve very young players and wins over Magnus Carlsen.

quizzes.title: Vaishali and the chess landscape
quizzes.passage: Indian Grandmaster R. Vaishali won the FIDE Women's Candidates Tournament 2026, held in Nicosia, Cyprus. She clinched the title by defeating Kateryna Lagno of Russia in the final round, finishing the event with 8.5 points out of 14. With this win she became the first Indian woman to claim the Candidates title. She will now challenge the reigning champion, Ju Wenjun of China, for the Women's World Chess Championship later in 2026. Her achievement comes in a strong period for Indian chess. Viswanathan Anand, often described as India's most successful chess player, has won the FIDE World Chess Championship several times. In 2024, Gukesh Dommaraju became the World Chess Champion, making him the second Indian to win the title after Anand. Koneru Humpy, India's highest-rated female chess player, has also won major honours in the sport. The sport itself is run globally by FIDE, the International Chess Federation. FIDE acts as the global governing authority for chess, oversees all major international competitions and sets the rules and rating standards that players follow. Its motto, Gens una Sumus, means 'We are One Family'. The World Chess Championship has a long history, with its first official champion crowned in the nineteenth century. Chess players from many countries take part in its events.

Consider the following statements:
I. Viswanathan Anand has won the FIDE World Chess Championship five times.

quizzes.title: India's recent chess results
quizzes.passage: Indian chess has produced a run of strong results in recent years. In 2024, the Indian men's and women's teams made history at the 45th Chess Olympiad by winning a gold medal, the first such gold for the country. The same year, Gukesh Dommaraju became the World Chess Champion after defeating Ding Liren of China. Later, he beat Magnus Carlsen in a classical game at Norway Chess 2025. Women's chess has also produced important results. Divya Deshmukh won the FIDE Women's World Cup 2025 by defeating Koneru Humpy in the final, and she became the third winner of the title. Humpy, India's highest-rated female chess player, has had a long career that includes a Women's World Rapid Chess Championship title. The junior ranks have also delivered results. GM Pranav Venkatesh won the FIDE World Junior Chess Championship 2025 in Montenegro, adding his name to the list of Indian champions in that event. Such wins show that Indian players are winning titles at several levels of the game. In 2025, Indian players also took part in top events such as Norway Chess. India also hosted the Chess World Cup 2025, a major event on the global calendar.
